_comment: The look the piece is wearing. /mosh-lab/tune writes this file with "publish look" and scripts/shade_bank.mjs reads it; nothing else decides what the footage looks like. It is config/composite.json - the lab's current default preset - with five changes made for production, each of which is a decision rather than a tweak. (1) fold on: foldIn 0.5, which folds inside the reveals rather than over the whole frame, so the fold acts where the damage map says and the still background is left alone. (2) curveBlend on: the hand-drawn damage curve is averaged with the word envelope instead of replacing it, so the concept words inside a clip drive that clip's own peaks. (3) underlayer.strength, the one dial that can take all of this to nothing: 0 is the footage untouched, 1 is everything here at the strength it describes. (4) feather 2 macroblocks / 6 frames: the damage's edge no longer stops at a block boundary - the ring of blocks around it repeats its damaged neighbours' motion vectors for a few frames, decaying outward, which is the same operation the two transitions perform on a whole frame. (5) dream off: DeepDream over the fold is built and measured and takes about three quarters of a second a frame on this card, which is a different piece from this one. The slot is here, the weights are cached, and turning it on re-shades the bank the same way any other dial does. The curve and the envelope are read across each bank clip's own length, so a three-second clip gets the whole shape rather than a slice of a thirty-second one.
